draft.title: Partnerships
card: A partnership is a business owned by two or more people. The owners are called partners.
Partners share the work of running the business. They also share the profits.
Partners share the debts too. If the business cannot pay what it owes, the partners are responsible for those debts.
Firms of lawyers, doctors and accountants are often partnerships. Each partner brings skills, and sometimes money, to the business.
draft.remember: A partnership has two or more owners who share the work, profits and debts.

opts: A vet clinic owned by three vets who share its profits
A bakery owned and run by one person, Ana
A café owned by one person who hires two staff
A shop with one owner and a paid manager
a.why: A partnership needs two or more owners, and the three vets share the profits. The other businesses each have one owner, even if they hire staff or a manager.
a.clue: Count the owners, not the workers.

b.q: Leila and Tom run a garden care business in Hobart. It loses money and owes a supplier $6000. Who is responsible for the debt?
opts: Leila and Tom share it
Leila alone, as she started it
Tom alone, as he bought the supplies
Nobody, as the business made no profit
b.why: In a partnership the partners share the debts as well as the profits. Leila and Tom are both owners, so both are responsible. Having no profit does not remove a debt.
b.clue: Partners share more than the profits.

a.best: A vet clinic owned by three vets who share its profits
